mood.summary: Nifty rose 0.65% to 23,146.15 and Sensex 0.56% to 74,729.27, a second day of gains, after a dip to 22,914 in the morning. The IT index jumped about 4% (Tech Mahindra +8.5%, TCS +4.9%, Infosys +4.6%), while private banks, FMCG, financials and oil & gas lagged and midcaps and smallcaps ended flat. Easing Brent ($105.5), a firmer rupee and calm volatility helped, but FIIs have sold for 15 straight sessions. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Yes Bank report on Saturday, PNB reported a ₹5,532 crore profit after the close, and the market is shut on Tuesday. Watch 23,077 as support and 23,229–23,373 as the next hurdle on Monday.

IT drove the gain with the IT index up about 4%: Tech Mahindra +8.48%, TCS +4.89% and Infosys +4.61%, while IndiGo (−1.91%) and BSE (−1.90%) led the losers.

The rally stayed narrow: only 26 Nifty stocks rose, midcaps and smallcaps ended flat, and FIIs have sold for 15 straight days (₹5,285 crore on Thursday).

news.headline: Sensex rises 414 points, Nifty ends at 23,146 as IT index jumps about 4%
news.summary: Sensex closed at 74,729.27 (+0.56%) and Nifty at 23,146.15 (+0.65%), a second day of gains, after dipping to 22,914 in early trade. Midcaps (−0.11%) and smallcaps (−0.01%) ended flat.
news.why: Nifty closed near the day's high and above the 23,077 hurdle; the next zone is 23,229–23,373, but Saturday's bank results decide Monday's tone.

news.headline: IT rally extends: Tech Mahindra +8.5%, TCS +4.9%, Infosys +4.6%, Wipro about +5.7%
news.summary: IT stocks led for a second day after Tech Mahindra's strong results and bonus. Infosys, Bharti Airtel and TCS added the most points to Nifty.
news.why: Big IT names are now up sharply in two days; Infosys reports on 23 Oct, so the rally will be tested by its numbers and US visa commentary.

news.headline: PNB Q2 profit ₹5,532 cr, up from ₹5,253 cr in Q1; gross NPA 2.55%
news.summary: Punjab National Bank's standalone profit rose about 5% from the June quarter to ₹5,532 crore; a year ago it was ₹4,904 crore. Gross NPA is 2.55%, net NPA 0.25%, and provision cover 97.3%.
news.why: Announced after the close, so Monday is the first reaction. Very clean asset quality supports PSU bank sentiment, but Saturday's private bank results will also move the sector.

news.headline: Indian Bank Q2 profit up 15% to ₹3,460 cr; NII +18%, net NPA 0.14%
news.summary: Indian Bank's profit rose 15% and net interest income 18%, with margin steady at 3.31%. It used gains from its NSE stake sale to add ₹1,390 crore to provisions. ICICI Securities raised its EPS estimates by about 4%.
news.why: Strong PSU bank numbers alongside PNB support the PSU bank pack into Saturday's private bank results.

news.headline: E2E Networks Q2 revenue up 411% to ₹224 cr; profit ₹72.7 cr
news.summary: The AI cloud company's revenue jumped 411% from a year ago and 43% from the June quarter, with a 32.5% profit margin. It repeated its ₹1,000 crore GPU contract with a sovereign AI client (first announced 1 Sept).
news.why: Results came near the close, so Monday shows the reaction. The share is volatile and has moved sharply on AI news before.

news.headline: Big bank results on Saturday: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, Yes Bank
news.summary: Analysts expect ICICI Bank profit +8–14% and Axis +37–43%, with margins under pressure after the RBI's rate hike. Yes Bank may disclose the AT1 ruling's impact.
news.why: These banks carry heavy Nifty weight; Monday's open will largely reflect their numbers, and Tuesday is a holiday.

news.headline: IndiGo, BSE and Max Healthcare top Nifty losers; private banks and FMCG lag
news.summary: InterGlobe Aviation fell 1.91%, BSE 1.90% and Max Healthcare 1.40%. Reliance was the biggest drag on Nifty in points.
news.why: The rally was narrow: only 26 Nifty stocks rose and 24 fell, so gains depend on a few large IT names.

news.headline: Tips Music jumps up to 7% as Q2 profit rises 24.5%; ₹6.50 dividend
news.summary: Profit rose to ₹66 crore and revenue 34.8% to ₹120 crore, though EBITDA margin slipped to 70.8% from 76%. The share hit ₹736.60.
news.why: Media was the second-best sector; the dividend record date was not stated.

news.headline: Solara Active Pharma rises 16% on turnaround to ₹28.6 cr profit
news.summary: Profit of ₹28.59 crore against a ₹9.29 crore loss a year ago. The share touched ₹759, near its 52-week high of ₹774.
news.why: Already up sharply; small pharma names can give back gains quickly.

news.headline: Jayaswal Neco profit doubles to ₹230 cr; revenue up 23%
news.summary: Q2 profit ₹229.81 crore vs ₹105.13 crore; revenue ₹2,194 crore vs ₹1,781 crore.

news.headline: Brent eases to $105.5, WTI $97.2 on talk of relaxed US shipping curbs
news.summary: Brent was down 0.42% and WTI 0.75% in Indian afternoon trade. Prices are still about 70% above a year ago.
news.why: Easing oil helps the rupee, inflation and oil marketing companies, but oil above $100 remains a pressure point for India.

news.headline: FIIs sell ₹5,285 cr for 15th straight day; DIIs buy ₹3,319 cr
news.summary: Foreign investors sold ₹5,285.37 cr in cash on the day Nifty crossed 23,000, while domestic institutions bought ₹3,319.39 cr.
news.why: Thursday's rally came without foreign buying; continued FII selling makes upside moves harder to hold.

news.headline: Tech Mahindra closes 8.5% higher at ₹1,790 after profit +32.7%, 1:1 bonus and ₹15 dividend
news.time: 15 Oct after close; move 16 Oct close
news.summary: Q2 profit rose 32.7% to ₹1,585.6 cr and revenue 15.6% to ₹16,180 cr, with deal wins of $1.02 bn. The board approved a 1:1 bonus and ₹15 interim dividend (record date 23 Oct). The share was up 6.8% to ₹1,762 at noon.
news.why: Stronger margins and deal wins counter Wipro's weak guide; the stock already rose 4.75% on Thursday ahead of the results.

news.headline: Federal Bank rises 2.9% on record Q2 profit of ₹1,386 cr, up 45%
news.summary: Federal Bank posted its highest-ever quarterly profit, up 45.1% from a year ago, and the share rose 2.9% to ₹344.80 on NSE.
news.why: A strong mid-size bank result sets a positive tone before HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis report on Saturday.

news.headline: Yes Bank crashes 14.5% after Supreme Court upholds quashing of ₹8,415 cr AT1 bond write-off
news.summary: After the Supreme Court upheld quashing of the ₹8,415 cr AT1 bond write-off (share −14.5% Thursday), estimates today put the hit to its core capital ratio at about 250 bps if the bonds are reinstated. Q2 results are due Saturday.
news.why: The size of any payout is not yet clear; Yes Bank's Q2 results on Saturday 17 Oct should give the first disclosure.

news.headline: Wipro guides Q3 revenue at −1.5% to +0.5%; large-deal bookings fall 59%
news.summary: Q2 profit fell 1.4% to ₹3,200.6 cr while revenue rose 9.1% to ₹24,750 cr. IT services revenue was flat in constant currency; total bookings fell 22.9% and large-deal bookings 58.6% from the June quarter. Operating margin was 16.5%. One live report said the share gained with the IT rally today, but no confirmed figure was found. Despite the weak guidance, the share rose about 5.7% on Friday with the IT rally (DSIJ).
news.why: The guidance points to no growth next quarter, which could cool Thursday's IT rally on Friday. Wipro closed +1.58% at ₹173.70 before the numbers.

news.headline: SEBI finalises closing auction: 3:30–3:40 PM session, F&O until 3:45 PM from 7 Dec
news.summary: SEBI set a 10-minute closing auction from 3:30 to 3:40 PM, derivatives trading until 3:45 PM (with some expiry exceptions), and expiring derivatives to settle on the average price of the last 30 minutes. Most changes start 7 Dec 2026; moving unexecuted limit orders into the auction starts 8 Feb 2027.
news.why: Mainly a change for traders and exchanges; capital-market stocks (BSE, Angel One, Nuvama) traded mixed, with BSE among the top losers today.

gold.label: Up ~0.6% today
gold.summary: MCX December gold closed 0.64% higher at ₹1,48,429 per 10g, with spot near $4,170 and silver up 1.33%, so gold ETFs like GOLDBEES ended firm. The rupee kept gaining (about 94.79 midday), which trims part of the rise for Indian buyers. MCX is just under ₹1,48,605 resistance (₹1,51,040 above, ₹1,46,400 support), and the 28 Oct Fed decision is the next big swing factor.
gold.how: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic gold rate: world gold in dollars × USD/INR, plus import duty. So both world events and the rupee move them.

scenarios.title: Dollar keeps sliding
scenarios.why: The dollar fully reversed its post-CPI spike and the US 10-year yield fell to about 5.1%. If that continues, world gold gains; a firmer rupee takes back a small part for Indian ETFs.
scenarios.when: Rupee 94.79 midday 16 Oct; DXY 102.00 on 15 Oct
scenarios.line: Dollar soft; MCX gold +0.64% to ₹1,48,429, rupee firmer.

scenarios.title: Fed holds on 28 Oct (~71% odds)
scenarios.why: Even after hot CPI and PPI, futures priced about a 71% chance of no change. A clear pause would keep yields and the dollar soft, helping gold toward $4,235. A firmer rupee would trim part of the gain in India.
scenarios.line: Yields and dollar ease; gold's best chance to clear $4,235.

scenarios.title: Fed hikes on 28 Oct (~29% odds)
scenarios.why: Hot September CPI (3.7%) briefly made a hike a coin-flip before odds fell back. A hike would push the dollar and US yields higher and could send gold back toward the $4,066 low. FII selling in India would likely rise too, weakening the rupee and cushioning part of the fall.
scenarios.line: Hot PPI (+1.3% m/m) keeps hike risk alive; gold toward $4,066.

scenarios.title: Gulf conflict widens, oil spikes
scenarios.why: Gold usually jumps on war fears, and higher oil weakens the rupee, so Indian gold ETFs gain on both counts. The catch: costly oil also feeds inflation and Fed-hike fears, which has capped gold's rallies recently, so gains can fade.
scenarios.line: Safe-haven buying plus a weaker rupee; can fade on inflation fears.

scenarios.title: US–Iran de-escalation
scenarios.why: Less war risk removes some safe-haven buying, though cheaper oil also lowers inflation and hike fears, which helps gold. The clearer effect for India is a stronger rupee, which pulls the rupee price of gold down.
scenarios.when: Reports on 15 Oct that the US may ease sanctions on West Asian crude shipping; no talks scheduled
scenarios.line: Less haven demand and a stronger rupee pull Indian gold down.

scenarios.title: Rupee slides past 97
scenarios.why: Every 1% fall in the rupee adds roughly 1% to Indian gold ETF prices even if world gold is flat. FII selling (14 straight days) and Brent above $100 are the pressures, but the rupee has gained five days in a row on RBI's steps and cheaper oil.
scenarios.when: USD/INR vs 97 (record low 96.96); now 95.05 close; daily FII flows; Brent
scenarios.line: Each 1% rupee fall adds ~1% to gold ETFs, even with gold flat.

scenarios.title: Rupee recovers
scenarios.why: The rupee has gained 183 paise in five sessions (to 95.05) on RBI support, cheaper oil and unwinding of dollar bets, a big reason MCX gold has lagged world gold. A further 2% recovery would knock about 2% off Indian gold ETFs.
scenarios.when: USD/INR ~94.79 midday 16 Oct after 95.05 on 15 Oct; support 94.70 (HDFC Securities)
scenarios.line: Rupee up ~1.9% in 5 days; another 2% would cut ~2% off gold ETFs.

scenarios.title: Stock market sell-off
scenarios.why: Investors move money into gold when stocks fall. The WGC says weak Indian equities drove gold ETF buying in September. In a severe crash gold can dip briefly as people sell everything to raise cash, then recover.
scenarios.when: Nifty 23,146 (+0.65%), second day up; midcaps flat; India VIX ~14
scenarios.line: Money shifts to gold when stocks fall; Saturday's bank results are the near-term test.

scenarios.title: Central banks keep buying
scenarios.why: China's central bank added 21 tonnes in September, its 23rd straight monthly purchase. Steady official buying tends to limit how far gold falls, though it rarely drives short-term moves.
scenarios.line: China added 21 t in Sept (23rd month); limits downside.

scenarios.title: India cuts import duty
scenarios.why: Indian gold ETFs track the domestic price, which includes customs duty. A duty cut would lower the Indian gold price, and ETF prices, overnight by about the size of the cut, as happened in the July 2024 Budget. A duty hike would do the opposite.
scenarios.line: Domestic gold, and ETFs, drop overnight by about the cut.

items.detail: CPPIB bought 10% of PHVL for ₹950 crore and another 5.79% through Series A CCPS for ₹550 crore. Money comes in at the subsidiary, so the parent's shares are not diluted.
items.holdNote: A big global investor valuing the unit is positive; realty was weak today, which can delay the reaction.

items.name: PFC (and REC)
items.head: RBI no-objection for the PFC–REC merger
items.detail: Clears a key approval for the merger; swap ratio and remaining approvals were not reported.
items.holdNote: Large PSU stocks move slowly on approvals; the swap ratio decides which share benefits more.

items.name: Tata Communications
items.head: Q2 profit +86% to ₹341 cr; EBITDA margin 21.3%; digital losses halve
items.detail: EBITDA ₹1,422 cr (+21%); revenue +9.6%; digital platforms +18.6%, data +12.2%. Digital margin improved to −3.6%.
items.holdNote: Clear beat, but it gave back half its intraday jump; better bought on a dip with a stop-loss.

items.name: Bharat Heavy Electricals
items.head: Q2 profit more than doubles to ₹810 cr; revenue +24%; ₹500 cr Haridwar expansion
items.detail: Revenue ₹9,300 cr (+23.8%), EBITDA ₹1,026 cr (+77%), margin 11% vs 7.7%. Board approved about ₹500 cr for thermal and nuclear equipment capacity and merging two units.
items.holdNote: Results beat estimates, but the stock is at a record and up 58% this year; NTPC's nuclear plans support the story. Buy only on a dip.

items.name: Tips Music
items.head: Q2 profit +24.5% to ₹66 cr; revenue +34.8%; ₹6.50 interim dividend
items.detail: EBITDA margin dipped to 70.8% from 76%. Record date not stated.
items.holdNote: Already up on the news; lower margin is the watch point.

items.name: Solara Active Pharma
items.head: Q2 profit ₹28.6 cr vs ₹9.3 cr loss a year ago
items.detail: Turnaround quarter; share near its 52-week high of ₹774.
items.holdNote: Small company already up sharply; late buyers risk a pullback.

items.name: Jayaswal Neco Industries
items.head: Q2 profit doubles to ₹230 cr; revenue ₹2,194 cr vs ₹1,781 cr
items.detail: Profit ₹229.81 cr vs ₹105.13 cr a year ago; revenue up about 23%.
items.holdNote: Strong numbers in a cyclical steel business; check Monday's reaction before acting.

items.name: Onward Technologies
items.head: Q2 profit up 41% to ₹16.8 cr; share hits 52-week high
items.detail: Small engineering-services firm; the share hit its 20% upper limit.
items.holdNote: Very small company and already up 20%; late buyers face high risk of a pullback.

items.name: Wipro
items.head: Q3 revenue guide −1.5% to +0.5%; profit −1.4%; large-deal bookings −59%
items.detail: Q2 profit ₹3,200.6 cr, revenue ₹24,750 cr (+9.1%). IT services flat in constant currency; total bookings $2,595 mn (−22.9% q/q), large deals $674 mn (−58.6%). Margin 16.5%.
items.move: Close about +5.7% with the IT rally (DSIJ)
items.holdNote: Shares rose with the sector despite weak guidance and bearish brokerages; that support is fragile.

items.name: Yes Bank
items.head: Supreme Court upholds quashing of ₹8,415 cr AT1 bond write-off; stock −14.5%
items.detail: Bondholders may reclaim their 2020 write-off of ₹8,415 cr. Analysts now estimate a ~250 bps hit to pro forma CET1; Tier-1 and total capital unaffected.
items.move: Thu close −14.5% to ₹18.12; today's move not found
items.holdNote: Results on Saturday should show the AT1 hit; review on Monday 19 Oct after the numbers.

items.name: Jio Financial Services
items.head: Q2 profit −51% to ₹340 cr, misses ₹470 cr estimate
items.detail: Income more than doubled but finance costs rose 325% as borrowing grew.
items.move: Among top 5 Nifty losers at close (Kotak Neo); −2.5% at 11:41 AM
items.holdNote: Brokerages including MOFSL cut FY27 estimates; estimate cuts tend to weigh for several sessions.

items.name: HDB Financial Services
items.head: Q2 profit +34% to ₹780 cr but below estimates; ₹2 dividend (record 23 Oct)
items.detail: Q2 profit +34% to ₹780 cr y/y but below estimates and slightly lower than last quarter; net interest margin down 12 bps. ₹2 dividend, record date 23 Oct.
items.holdNote: Two days of heavy selling to a record low; avoid until it stabilises.

items.name: Nestlé India
items.head: Shares fall 7.8% despite Q2 profit +36% to ₹1,026.7 cr
items.detail: Sales +20.5% to ₹6,782 cr, EBITDA +31%; roughly in line with estimates after a 6% run-up this month. Management flagged food inflation and cost pressure.
items.holdNote: Down about 9% in two days; selling has not settled yet.

items.name: Persistent Systems
items.head: Q2 profit falls 25% to ₹351.5 cr on Nagarro takeover costs; revenue up to ₹4,663.9 cr
items.detail: Revenue rose from ₹3,580.7 cr as Nagarro SE (94% acquired) was added; integration and financing costs cut profit from ₹471.5 cr. Corporate guarantee of up to €1,540 mn for bridge loans; up to $1.25 bn fund-raise approved on 5 Oct.
items.holdNote: Company calls the margin hit temporary, but a profit fall at a premium valuation usually gets sold first.

items.name: HDFC Life Insurance
items.head: Q2 profit +13.6% to ₹508 cr, below estimates; APE +11%
items.detail: Premium growth was healthy but profit missed; board also cleared up to ₹500 cr of subordinated NCDs.
items.move: −1.63% to ₹541.55 at noon; close not found
items.holdNote: Market rejected the profit miss even though brokerages stay positive; wait for it to settle.

guide._all: Each card is a company-specific event from the latest filings and news. Green = likely to support the share, red = likely to pressure it, amber = watch. New today: PNB reported after the close (fresh, not yet priced), E2E Networks reported near the close, plus Indian Bank, Tips Music, Solara and Jayaswal Neco results. DLF, LTM, Oberoi Realty, Urban Company and others report this evening; they will appear in Monday's morning update. No client-loss or order-cancellation news found today. Review-by dates are counted in trading days (20 Oct is a market holiday).
guide.Can rise: Positive triggers. A share does not always rise on good news, especially if it ran up before the announcement or the overall market is weak.
guide.Can fall: Negative triggers. Results misses, big investor exits and weak business updates usually hit the share on the day and can weigh for weeks.
guide.Order won: An order matters most when it is big compared with the company's yearly revenue (5–10% or more is significant for smaller companies). Repeat orders and orders in a new area are good signs of future growth. Check the execution period: a 24-month order adds revenue slowly. Being named the only qualified bidder (Goodluck) is a step before an order, not an order itself.
guide.Results: Shares react to results versus expectations, not just growth. Profit growing slower than sales signals squeezed margins, in-line results after a run-up often get sold (Nestle), and guidance for the next quarter can matter more than the quarter itself (Wipro). The earnings call commentary often matters as much as the numbers.
guide.Business update: Monthly sales, pre-sales and festive data give an early read on the quarter before results come out.
guide.Board decision: Board outcomes that usually lift a share: buyback, bonus, stock split, special dividend, demerger or merger that simplifies the group. Ones that can pressure it: big equity fund raise (QIP or rights issue) that adds new shares, large acquisitions that need fresh capital (Aegis), or large related-party deals.
guide.Stake sale: When a promoter or big investor sells in a block deal, the share often falls on the day because the sale is at a discount. If quality institutions buy, it usually recovers within weeks.
guide.Regulatory: For pharma: a USFDA warning letter or import alert is a big negative, while a Form 483 with a few procedural observations (Dr Reddy's) is usually minor. Approvals, certifications and cuts in tax demands (Paytm) are positives; new or higher tax demands (Mphasis) and lawsuits (Bank of Baroda) are negatives, though most are disputed for years. Rule changes by NPCI, SEBI or the exchanges (UPI fees, F&O exits) can move a whole group of stocks.
guide.Management change: A sudden exit of a CEO or CFO can spook investors; a planned succession usually doesn't.
guide.Corporate action: Takeovers, open offers and delisting plans. These change who owns the company and can create short-term price moves. If the share already trades above the deal price (IDBI Bank), the upside depends on the open-offer terms.
guide.Fund raise: Debt or government loans don't dilute shareholders. Equity raises (QIP, rights, preferential issue) add new shares and can weigh on the price.
guide.Legal claim: A lawsuit or legal claim against a company. A big headline number can hit the share for days, but most claims take years and are often dismissed or settled for far less. Watch whether the court admits the case and what the company files.

items.title: India–US trade deal
items.who: Commerce Ministry and US Trade Representative
items.latest: On 15 Oct Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the first tranche of the deal has been finalised and is in legal drafting, and India will operationalise it once it gets a competitive edge over peer countries. US Ambassador Sergio Gor said the two sides are very close (Bloomberg). No tariff details have been released.
items.effect: A deal that lowers US tariffs would help exporters that depend on the US: textiles and apparel, gems and jewellery, auto parts, chemicals, seafood. Failure or new tariffs would hit the same group.
items.when: First tranche: legal drafting under way; signing date not fixed
items.likely: Medium to high: first tranche finalised per the minister, but not yet signed
items.watch: Signing date and tariff details for textiles, gems, auto parts and chemicals

items.title: US Federal Reserve rate decision
items.latest: After hot September CPI (3.7%) and PPI (+1.3% m/m), markets price about a 72% chance of a hold on 28 Oct, but Goodreturns reports December hike odds near 92%. US 10-year yield ~5.10% today after a 10 bps fall Thursday. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks before the meeting.
items.effect: A hold is mildly positive for Indian stocks, the rupee and gold. A surprise hike would lift the dollar and US yields, push FIIs to sell more, and hurt IT and gold.
items.likely: Hold likely (~72%) in October; December hike odds reported near 92%
items.watch: Warsh speech, US jobs data; next CPI in November

items.title: RBI rate decision: another hike likely in December
items.latest: RBI hiked the repo rate to 5.50% on 7 Oct. September CPI came in at 5.54% (above the 5.4% forecast). HDFC Bank, DBS, Oxford Economics and others now expect 25 bps more in December; some see 50–75 bps more this year.
items.effect: A hike raises borrowing costs: negative for rate-sensitive stocks such as NBFCs, real estate and autos, and for bond prices. Banks can gain on margins at first. A pause would be a relief rally trigger.
items.likely: High for a 25 bps hike, based on economist forecasts

items.title: IDBI Bank sold to Fairfax (60.72% stake at ₹81/share)
items.latest: On 14 Oct the Cabinet approved Fairfax's ₹52,878 cr bid: the government sells 30.48% and LIC 30.24% at ₹81 a share. IDBI jumped 9% to ₹90.39 on 14 Oct, then fell 8.1% to ₹83.07 on 15 Oct. Fairfax reportedly plans to combine IDBI Bank, Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital into one group. On 16 Oct Business Standard reported Fairfax proposes contributing Digit Insurance and IIFL Capital to IDBI Bank; CSB Bank denied merger talks with IDBI.
items.effect: Largest privatisation since Air India and a boost to reform sentiment. For IDBI shareholders, the stock already trades above ₹81; open-offer terms for public shareholders are not yet announced, so chasing the jump is risky. Fairfax must merge or exit CSB Bank, where it owns 40%.
items.likely: High (approved); RBI fit-and-proper and CCI clearances still needed
items.watch: Open-offer price and size; RBI approval; government's plan to sell its remaining 15%

items.title: Scrap LTCG tax on shares (and possibly cut STT)
items.who: Proposed by SBI Research · Decision: Finance Ministry
items.latest: SBI Research (12 Oct) proposed scrapping long-term capital gains tax on equities, with a 2–3 year holding period, to stem FPI outflows of ₹3.04 lakh cr this year. On 14 Oct the Finance Minister said it is 'too early to comment' and announced no change.
items.effect: If done, a big positive for the whole market and for FPI flows; brokers, exchanges and AMCs would gain most. Current LTCG is 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh. A cut in STT on F&O (raised to 0.05% on futures in April) would mainly help brokers and BSE.
items.likely: Low to medium: equity LTCG brought in about ₹1.29 lakh cr, hard to give up with a ~4.5% fiscal deficit
items.watch: Pre-Budget consultations (Nov–Jan) and any Finance Ministry comment

items.title: SEBI closing auction for the final price
items.latest: SEBI finalised the rules on 15 Oct: a 10-minute closing auction from 3:30 to 3:40 PM on all trading days, index and stock derivatives trading until 3:45 PM (some expiring index contracts excepted), and expiring derivatives settled on the volume-weighted average price of the last 30 minutes.
items.effect: Changes how the closing price is set. Mainly affects traders, index funds and exchanges; little effect on long-term holders. BSE was among today's top Nifty losers (−1.8%).
items.when: Most changes from 7 Dec 2026; limit/iceberg orders into the auction from 8 Feb 2027
items.watch: Exchange circulars and broker system changes

items.title: 0.4% UPI merchant fee on payments above ₹2,000
items.latest: On 13 Oct NPCI deferred the 0.4% merchant discount rate on certain UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000 until after Diwali; a new date will be notified.
items.effect: A fee on large UPI merchant payments would give payment companies a revenue source; small merchants would bear the cost. Positive for payment firms such as Paytm when it starts.
items.when: After Diwali (8 Nov); new date to be notified
items.watch: NPCI circular with the start date

items.title: US midterm elections and Iran risk
items.latest: Midterms are on 3 Nov. President Trump said there will be no US strike on Iran before then. The Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted, but on 15 Oct reports said the US is weighing easing sanctions on West Asian crude shipping, pulling Brent toward $104.
items.effect: After 3 Nov the Iran pledge expires, so oil and safe-haven risk could rise. Higher oil hurts India (rupee, inflation, oil marketing companies, paints, airlines) and helps gold and upstream oil.

items.title: OPEC+ oil output for December
items.latest: On 4–5 Oct OPEC+ kept November output unchanged. The next monthly decision (for December) is due in early November.
items.effect: Higher output would ease crude and help India's rupee, inflation and oil marketing companies. A cut would do the opposite.
items.watch: Brent near $103.7–104 (15 Oct); US sanctions easing on tankers

items.title: More PSU stake sales (OFS) this year
items.latest: About ₹55,757 cr raised so far in FY27 from stake sales in 9 PSUs (including LIC and Coal India). With IDBI, receipts cross the ₹80,000 cr target for the first time in 8 years. The government may sell its residual IDBI stake in the market.
items.effect: An offer-for-sale (OFS) is usually priced at a discount, so the PSU stock often dips for a few days around the sale. Meeting the target can reduce pressure for further big sales this year.
items.when: Through March 2027; OFS dates are announced a day ahead
items.watch: OFS announcements on NSE/BSE (usually the evening before)

items.title: GST process reforms
items.latest: The GST Council approved process reforms at its 8 Oct meeting to speed decisions and cut compliance; the Prime Minister welcomed them. Details of each change are still being notified.
items.effect: Lower compliance cost helps small businesses and consumer companies over time; no immediate rate change.

items.title: Union Budget 2027
items.latest: Preparations are under way. The LTCG/STT debate, disinvestment, capex and the fiscal deficit (~4.5% of GDP) will be the key themes.
items.effect: Tax changes on capital gains or STT, customs duty on gold, and capex plans can move whole sectors on the day.
items.watch: Pre-Budget meetings and leaks from December
